summary: Earth Analog Explorer is an interactive web platform designed to bridge Earth science and space exploration by identifying and analyzing terrestrial geological analogues that mimic the extreme environments of the Moon and Mars. Integrating NASA's official resources and open data, our platform equips researchers and space enthusiasts with advanced analytical tools. Key features include an analog similarity index to quantitatively measure environmental matching, machine-specific analog matching to tailor sites for specific mission parameters, and an intuitive split-screen comparison view to evaluate side-by-side geological metrics. By streamlining how mission planners select and validate terrestrial testing grounds for rovers and habitats, Earth Analog Explorer makes planetary research more accessible, visual, and data-driven.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

Earth Analog Explorer (earth-analog-explorer.vercel.app) maps Earth-based geological sites that mimic the extreme environments of the Moon and Mars.

Integrating NASA's official resources, the platform features:

Analog Similarity Index: Quantitatively scores how closely an Earth site matches a lunar or Martian target zone.

Machine-Specific Analog Matching: Filters optimal testing grounds tailored to specific rovers, landers, or human habitats.

Split-Screen Comparison: Displays side-by-side environmental and geological metrics for direct comparison.

Benefits & Impact

Selecting accurate terrestrial testing sites is essential before launching space hardware. Our tool streamlines site selection for researchers, mission planners, and educators—making planetary analog data visual, mission-focused, and easy to verify through direct links to NASA documentation.
